page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supporting 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is limited, scoring in the bottom 25% on both stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth falling into the bottom 10% and large block read/write bandwidth in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and compression tasks show moderate capability, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the middle 50%.

The c2d-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Due to its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, it is positioned for workloads requiring larger memory footprints relative to compute capacity. However, the poor database operations and redis SET performance (both in the bottom 10%) indicate it is less optimal for high-throughput transactional databases. Suitable workloads include lightweight memory-cached applications, single-threaded data processing, and basic web serving.
